solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine letting on quietly

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the letting word after the quiet sign, building onto it

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly
letting a property is leasing it

explanation.surface: Someone admits, with relief, that they quietly let the cat out of the bag and it went fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fine is agreeable or satisfactory, an ordinary synonym for pleasant.

clue.text: Mess about with branch in flower

parts.note: to lark is to fool or mess about
a spur is a side branch, as of a railway or road

explanation.surface: A gardener fiddles with a stem bearing a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a delphinium-like garden plant with tall flower spikes, an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Realtors go crazy for expert on houses

indicators.note: crazy tells us the letters of realtors go behave wildly and rearrange

explanation.surface: Estate agents go wild over a property specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Realtors deal in houses, but here 'houses' are the twelve divisions of the zodiac chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Horoscope casters read the twelve celestial houses, a specialist sense of house in astrology.

clue.text: Favour clue ending in anagram

indicators.note: the clue states plainly that the words clue ending are to be put in an anagram

explanation.surface: A solver asks for a kindness: a hint at the end of an anagram clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgence is a special favour or privilege granted, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Grand drunk getting excited

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
ripped is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A grand old man, plastered, becomes worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gripped by something means being thrilled or held in suspense, close to stirred up.

clue.text: Just one entering distant expo

definitions.meaning: an expo or exhibition is a trade show, the second definition

indicators.note: entering means the numeral goes inside the word for distant

parts.note: far means distant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Only one person turns up at a far-off exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions bracket the wordplay: Just at the start and expo at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair both mean impartial, giving each side its due.

clue.text: High time embracing Greek character's dance

indicators.note: embracing means the jumbled time letters wrap around the Greek letter
high means intoxicated, so the letters of time are muddled

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: It's about time a Greek person joined the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' scrambles TIME into MIET, which then embraces NU.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a slow stately ballroom step for couples, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Scripture lesson books to deliver without regular charge

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
to free someone is to deliver them

explanation.surface: A Bible class covers books that bring salvation free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Living somewhere with no rent payable means no periodic payment to the landlord.

clue.text: Journey round old trailers along the way

indicators.note: the journey word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a ride is a journey
film trailers are advertisements, ADS

explanation.surface: A trip past aged trailers parked beside the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailers' looks like vehicles beside the road but means previews, i.e. adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated along the way stands at the edge of the route, beside the highway.

clue.text: Scraped a result worse than an F

definitions.meaning: cheese that has been scraped against a rasp has been shredded this way

definitions.text: a result worse than an F
definitions.meaning: graded G, a letter below F in an A-to-G marking scale

explanation.surface: A student just scraped through, though the mark looks even worse than a fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as G-RATED: a mark one letter beyond F, so a worse result.
explanation.definitionFit: Grated food has been scraped against a rough surface, a plain synonym in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: High society leading couple away from sink with constant decay

indicators.note: the first two letters of the sinking word are dropped

parts.note: to scupper a ship is to sink it
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rust is decay of iron

explanation.surface: Posh society's top pair flee a sink caked in persistent grime.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping SC from the front of SCUPPER leaves UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocracy are proverbially the top layer of the loaf, a common idiom for the elite.

clue.text: Work with a large gem

parts.note: OP is opus, a musical work
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A jeweller labours over a big precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a precious stone with shifting iridescent colours, so an example of a gem.

clue.text: Sign of maturity? Comparatively less lustrous nous

parts.note: grey hair is a mark of advancing age; the query flags the loose definition
matter means more matt, less shiny

explanation.surface: Greying hair and a duller sheen hint that age brings wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain tissue is used figuratively for intelligence, so the phrase means common sense or brains.

clue.text: Notes ruin, mother's ruin, a mounting trouble

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin

indicators.note: mounting, in a down clue, means the trouble word reads upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Jottings about a mother sinking into ruinous gin drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is British slang for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are notes scribbled in the margins of a book, so a plural of jottings.

clue.text: Guide once to extend by several inches

parts.note: to tender is to offer or extend, as a hand
a foot is twelve inches

explanation.surface: An old Girl Guide manual explains lengthening something a few inches.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenderfoot was the novice rank in the Scouts and Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was formerly the rank of a newly joined Scout or Guide, so a novice member of the movement.

clue.text: Sibling with problem returning shoes

parts.note: bro is informal for brother

indicators.note: returning means the word for the problem is read backwards

parts.note: a snag is a problem

explanation.surface: A brother has trouble taking back footwear to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Brogans are heavy ankle-high work boots, an example of footwear.

clue.text: City growth — a blight

parts.note: a bud is new growth on a plant
a pest is a blight or nuisance

explanation.surface: Urban development is condemned as a blot on the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, an example of a major city.

clue.text: What constitutes danger, when exploding close to one?

definitions.text: What constitutes danger, when exploding close to one?

indicators.note: exploding scatters the letters of the word danger into a new order
the close of a word is its final letter, here of one

explanation.surface: A question about what makes something perilous if it blows up near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when exploding' rearranges DANGER; the close of 'one' adds E. The whole clue also describes the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is exactly what is perilous when it bursts near someone.

clue.text: Separate record and notes

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
re and te are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A record kept apart from the written notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct or individually separate, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Liberal turning to name in stupid testimony

indicators.note: turning to says one letter changes into another

parts.note: witless means stupid

explanation.surface: A Liberal names a culprit in a foolish court statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to give evidence, so the noun can mean testimony.

clue.text: Fiat for the time being desire nice motoring

indicators.note: the words desire nice are driven around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone currently longs for a pleasant drive in a Fiat car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat looks like the Italian car, prompted by 'motoring'; here it means a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: In English divorce law this was the provisional court order, not final until made absolute.

clue.text: What's sung in church examination?

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective: describing music sung by a choir

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A query about hymns performed during a church test.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music for voices in a choir, the kind of thing that is sung.

clue.text: With Conservative ousted, pack in facility

indicators.note: ousted means that letter is thrown out of the stopping word

parts.note: to pack in something is to stop or cease it

explanation.surface: A Tory is expelled and a building is shut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility means effortlessness or skill, a synonym of naturalness in doing something.

clue.text: Hype needing a thorough looking at, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a proper gander is slang for a good long look

explanation.surface: Publicity that demands careful inspection, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is British slang for a look, so a 'proper gander' is a thorough one.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional information that exaggerates or misleads is hype, near synonyms for slanted publicity.

clue.text: Delight in single entry

indicators.note: in says the answer is lodged within the words single entry

explanation.surface: Pleasure in a solo entrance or a lone diary note.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great joy or merriment, a synonym of delight.

clue.text: Can former nurse let go?

parts.note: can and loo are both slang for a toilet
SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a now-discontinued British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A question whether an ex-nurse is able to release her grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb 'is able to' but is the noun, a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken one's grip or untie something is to release it, a sense of letting go.

clue.text: Courses in which you'll get soup in some otherwise unhelpful places?

definitions.text: Courses in which you'll get soup in some otherwise unhelpful places?

parts.words: Courses in which you'll get soup in some otherwise unhelpful places?
parts.note: soup is an opening dish of a meal; non-___ are unhelpful ideas, so the same word names the first course and places that help

explanation.surface: A diner asks which dishes serve soup in otherwise poor restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening dishes of a meal, often soup, are named for being first in the run of courses.

clue.text: Briefs look carefully at couples

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
ties means joins or couples, as a verb

explanation.surface: A lawyer reviews legal documents concerning pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' looks like legal papers but is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are short underpants, and this word is a jokey name for skimpy knickers.
